summary: The F₂ relaxation is exactly Lemma GT1 in Z52_BANKED.md §1(b) (PROVED relative to Dirichlet: every non-square n ≡ 1 (4) has a level 4r at which no odd real character mod 4r obstructs; checked with the same 'v(−1) ∈ span' test in scripts/z52_bank_gt1.py). SYNTHESIS_SPARKS9 Prop 2.2 frees only χ_{−t}. I recomputed it (EVIDENCE). For p ≤ 2·10⁴ and C ≤ 100, the relaxation holds for 31.4% of (p,C) pairs and the full condition holds in 13.8% of those. For p ≤ 10⁵ and C ≤ 40 the figures are 35.9% and 29.9%. Every prime has a genus-free C ≤ 13, and the (★)-failures 409, 577, 5569, 9601 and 19141 (C ≤ 100) are genus-free at 21–30 levels each, so (★) failures are not genus failures. Caveat: a key-term grep accidentally showed Haiku's ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO line for this item before I computed.
next: None: the genus layer is settled. The remaining question is the class of the divisor inside the square class of −1 (P(full | relaxation) ≈ 0.14–0.30).

summary: Literature check (Huang–Liu–Rudnick arXiv:1903.04005, intro). Asymptotics for Gaussian prime angles hold in sectors of width > X^{−3/10+ε} (Ricci). Harman–Lewis (Mathematika 48, 2001) prove existence in narrower sectors by a sieve. GRH gives X^{−1/2+ε}, and X^{−1/2} is a hard floor because of 'forbidden regions'. The fixed-p ES angle conditions sit in tubes of width ≍ 1/p (BRAINSTORM/canonical_invariants.md Prop C; y3_salie_angle.md), below that floor, so even GRH sector equidistribution cannot see them. The repo already uses Hecke sector equidistribution only for family-level results (DISCOVERIES (J) Cor 3.4).

I derived the interval. At level C the certificate divisor is d = 4Cu − 1 ∈ [4C − 1, √(4Cp+1)], with modulus s = 4C. Lenstra/CHN (s ≥ N^{1/3}) apply iff C ≳ √p/4, and there they give only an O(1) upper bound with enumeration, never existence. Heuristically about 1/4 of the expected mass lies at C ≥ √p. Measured (EVIDENCE): 41%, 31% and 31% of the ordered (★) solutions at p ≈ 10⁵, 10⁶ and 10⁷ (15 primes each) lie at Lenstra-regime levels, with at most 2 per level. The repo already records that this tool gives upper bounds and enumeration only (B2_ACROSS_FIELDS row 8, gon_lll_relation_lattice (b1), polynomial_method.md).

The exact measurement already exists: BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md summary item 3 (scripts/z52b_dividing_indep.py) found observed/independent survivors = 8.5·10⁵ at X = 1000. I went one level further (EVIDENCE): I stratified the same residue model by the Legendre vector of N at q = 11..31 (128 strata, 2·10⁵ samples). The ratio fell from 448 to 8.5 at X = 316 and from 9.5·10⁵ to 148 at X = 1000. So about 2/3 of the log-correlation between certificate families is the shared quadratic-character (sign-layer) pattern, consistent with the lane's 'difficulty tracks n(p)'.
next: If wanted: add Legendre symbols at more primes (or condition on n(p)) to see whether the residual ratio → O(1); then the residue model is 'independent given the sign pattern'.

summary: The one-parameter form re-indexes the trial form of PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1. I proved and checked that on the arc m ∈ (p/q, p/(q−1)], r_p(m) = qm − p and every win there has B = q. On p < 3000 that is 1497 wins with 0 mismatches. So the 'arcs where r_p(m) is small' are exactly the B-lines of the pair form, entered at small u: no new structure. 409 has no win on any arc with m ≤ p + 1. The Voronoi/exponential-sum reading is the Dirichlet-hyperbola count at Planck scale again.

Read erdosproblems.com/314. The problem asks for the minimal ε(n) = Σ_{n≤k≤m} 1/k − 1 and whether liminf n²ε(n) = 0. Lim–Steinerberger (arXiv:2405.11354) solved it using the continued fraction of e plus Heilbronn-type bounds on ‖n²θ‖. The extremal examples come from Diophantine approximation of a constant; they carry no 'reciprocal-sum multiplicities' and no count distribution to compare with R(p). The connection is nominal.

Verified the closing claim (PROVED, elementary): a positive cone P of an ordered ring contains 1 = 1² and is closed under +, so P ⊇ ℕ, and Z has a unique ordering. The meaningful variants (restricted positive cones/semigroups) are covered in BRAINSTORM/other_rings.md (positive cone C ⊂ R), ff_erdos_straus.md (monic cone) and the z52b_analogues constraint worlds.

Read Dagal (arXiv:2003.13229, math.HO). Its Thm 5.1 rewrites 1/s + 1/(rs) = 1/(qr) + 1/(qs) with r = q + d and s = qr − d. That is two terms to two terms with the same sum, so it only permutes the finite solution set of 4/p and cannot produce existence. I applied it to all 1559 unordered solutions for primes p < 300 (CERTIFIED): it applies in only 2 cases (it needs z = r·y and (r+1) | (y+r)). Both images are already-known solutions; one switches Type I/II.

PROVED: for a prime p ≡ 1 (4), no solution of 4/p has a repeated denominator. 2/a + 1/b = 4/p forces (2a′ − 1) | p or (4b′ − 1) | p, hence 4 | p + 1. So the ordered count is 6 × unordered = 6 × increasing; the MO229514 'distinct' convention differs from ET's ordered count by exactly the factor 6. Checked on 95 primes < 1200 (0 repeats) and tabulated the Type I/II split.

Computed E = {odd n ≤ 10⁶ : R(n) = 0} for the C-form/(★) line (CERTIFIED): 980 elements, namely all 499 odd squares plus 481 non-squares (197 ≡ 1 mod 4), 239 of them in [10⁵, 10⁶], so the composite exceptions are not sporadic. None of the hypothesised closure properties hold. 409·k ∉ E for k ∈ {3, 5, 7, 9, 25, 49, 81, 121, 577} (R = 4–34). Scaling n → n·m² keeps an exception in only 12 of 2336 cases. Products of two exceptions are exceptions in only 62 of 2267 cases. There are no infinite non-square square-class families of the form 409·m².

This is a publication/community deliverable, not a mathematical step. The content already exists as structured text (FRONTIER §3: statement · scope · rules out · does NOT rule out · pointer; §6 dead ends; B2_ACROSS_FIELDS tables). Exporting it as a CSV/web page is mechanical, and whether to publish is the user's call.

Reproduced the Carmichael ratios U/median(n ± 4k, k ≤ 5): 2.86–5.91 (EVIDENCE; U computed with my own C counter, validated against brute force). The hardest primes < 1500 have ratio 0.06–0.09 (1201, 241, 1009, 421, 1321, 193, …). Semiprime medians: hard×hard 0.23, residue-matched control (p, q ≡ 1 mod 24) 0.25, unmatched mid×mid 0.30, easy×easy 0.57. 193·241: U = 367 against a neighbour median of 1720.5 (0.21). So hardness does not compound beyond the residue-class (≡ 1 mod 24) effect, though one hard×hard product (1009·1321) is as low, at 0.06, as the hardest primes.

Did the chart computation. In the Cremona chart (u, v, w) = (1/x, 1/y, 1/z) the ES cubic becomes the plane u + v + w = 4/n. The three lines at infinity of the Cayley cubic 4xyz = n·t(xy + yz + zx) go to the toric triangle uvw = 0. The denominator-zero curves (the coordinate axes through the affine node) go to the three points (4/n, 0, 0), …, and the affine node goes to the line at infinity. The repo already has this log-CY/boundary picture: BRAINSTORM/rational_to_integral_cubic.md M2 (nodes, mod-p reduction = toric boundary, Type I/II = strata), cayley_markoff_cm.md (the ES boundary triangle passes through three nodes) and BL's log K3 framing (B2_ACROSS_FIELDS row 6).

Concretely, CRT-combining valid congruence conditions for ES (taking the union of identity families mod 3, 5, 7, 8, …) is Mordell's covering, which leaves exactly the 6 square classes mod 840 (FRONTIER §1). Minimising the CRT representative of an intersection is irrelevant, since any one condition suffices. Mordell–Schinzel/B1 (POINTWISE_SIZE Thm M) shows no finite combination covers the square classes. The item has no ES content beyond this.
